page.layout: One column of running text, with three marginal notes in the right margin. No notes in the left margin. A Greek line and a Latin line in smaller type stand below the text.

main_text.head: Alterum militaris virtutis calcar, praemia.
main_text.p: Non enim cogi tantum & metu impelli vult, erigi vult & laude excitari. Eodem praemii quo severitatis autore, Rufus Helfius gregarius miles servati civis decus retulit, donatusque est ab Apronio torquibus & hasta Casar[?] addidit civicam coronam. Tramia.Nostris mori-bus milites magis auri & argenti pondere, quam herbida aut oleastri corona, delectantur. Caeterum poe-nae & praemiorum gravitate non alius magis, isto quidem aevo, Wallesteinio Wallesk[?] exercitum diversi hominum generis continuisse memoratur, quanquam major de saevitia ejus, quam largitione militari, rumor orbem pervasit.
main_text.head: Spargere bellum, est aut causae aut viribus diffidentis.
main_text.p: Causae: dum praedae magis cogendae, quam debellando certamini, incumbas. Viribus: dum percul-sos in aciem producere non audeas. Utrumque de Tacfarinate Tacfarinas. memoratur, qui praedae intentus, pugnam velocitate devitans, ea ratione irritum fessumque Romanum impune ludificabatur. Quod genus militiae, si cum gravis armaturae hoste tibi mobili res fuerit, non est omnino aspernandum. Sic ante in eadem Numidia Jugurtha duces Romanos diu ludificabatur. Sic Parthi equestres Romanis, Sueonum agminibus Poloni, damno aut taedio fuerunt.
main_text.head: Plurimae lites ex habendi cupidi-tate.
main_text.p: Quae bellorum frequentissima, eadem & litium in foro creberrima materies.

page.notes: The Greek line below the text could not be read letter by letter, so it is marked illegible. "Cafar" is printed with a long s that reads as f; transcribed as Casar[?], since the printed form may also be Caesar. "fervati" read as servati (long s). "eft" read as est. "Tramia" and "Wallesk" are marginal notes whose exact forms are uncertain; the marginal mark after "Tramia" may be a symbol. "i. c." read as i. e. Italic passage in the second paragraph ("irritum fessumque...") confirmed as italic; the word "Quod genus militiae" may be italic in print but was set as roman here.
